meta.title: LibreRythmo: free dubbing studio, rythmo band and voice recording
meta.description: LibreRythmo is a free, open-source dubbing studio. Design the rythmo band frame by frame, record the voices on top, mute one character to act their part, and export the dubbed video. Windows, macOS and Linux.
meta.keywords: rythmo band, dubbing studio, free dubbing software, dubbing recording, rythmo band editor, dubbing software, lip sync, DETX, fandub, remove vocals, dubbing transcription, open source dubbing

hero.title: The simple, free dubbing studio.
hero.subtitle: Design the rythmo band frame by frame, then record the voices right on top of it. You can even mute one character to act their part, then export the dubbed video. **Free**, **fast**, **no video size limit**. Windows, macOS and Linux.

what.title: Design the band, then record the voices.
what.body: A rythmo band is the text that scrolls under the picture in dubbing studios, stretched so each word lands on the actor's lips. LibreRythmo first lets you build it, frame by frame. Since version 3, it also records: each actor lays their takes right on the band, and the video comes out dubbed. All free, with no duration limit.

features.title: Their voice mutes, the rest of the mix keeps playing.
features.body: Mute a character: during their lines, their voice disappears, but the music, effects and other actors stay. You perform inside the real soundtrack, not on top of it. The instrumental track is made locally by the built-in voice remover.
features.alt: LibreRythmo dubbing monitor: one character's voice muted onto the voiceless track

features.title: One character, one track, as many takes as you need.
features.body: The band scrolls like the final render, and you record from the playhead. Takes of the same pass stack up: you keep the best one, trim it, move it. Microphone latency is corrected so the voice lands exactly where you performed it, and an FX button cleans the sound (EQ, de-esser, compression, level).
features.alt: LibreRythmo recording mode: takes per character under the rythmo band

features.title: The video comes out dubbed.
features.body: On export, LibreRythmo mixes the recorded voices into a GPU-encoded MP4. The band can stay burned in or drop out, to deliver the dubbed video alone. For interchange: import DETX, SRT / ASS / VTT and YouTube; export DETX, subtitles, PDF documents and a ZIP of the recordings.
features.alt: LibreRythmo MP4 export window with recordings mix and GPU encoding

features.title: Every word snapped to the frame.
features.body: Each word boundary lands on the lips, down to the frame, and the magnet catches edges to speed things up. Need to fix several lines at once? Multi-selection changes the character, font or voice-over in one go. All across 1 to 4 tracks.
features.alt: Frame-accurate word adjustment on the LibreRythmo rythmo band

features.title: Smooth scrubbing, even in 4K or HEVC.
features.body: The wheel scrolls the band along the audio, frame by frame, without a single hitch. In the background, a 720p proxy makes any source instant, whatever the codec. The export starts over from the full-quality original.
features.alt: LibreRythmo fullscreen playback with the composited rythmo band

features.title: One-key reacs, fonts in the project.
features.body: A reac (ah, oh, fff, (laughs)…) drops in with one key, a line switches to underlined voice-over, and each actor has their own colour, picked with keys 1 to 9. Any line can carry its own font too: any TTF/OTF embeds into the project, which stays shareable as-is.
features.alt: Character panel and reac palette in LibreRythmo

features.title: The text starts straight from the audio.
features.body: Retyping a whole episode takes hours. Transcription listens to the audio and pre-fills the lines, detecting the voices to create one character per actor. It all runs locally: the engine and models install in one click, only if you want them.
features.alt: LibreRythmo assisted transcription window with model and language choice

features.title: Automatic shot detection, live stats.
features.body: LibreRythmo spots shot changes on its own and drops the markers on the timeline. Scene slicing shows the line count, duration and characters live. OUT segments flag the stretches with nothing to dub.
features.alt: Scene markers and shot detection on the LibreRythmo timeline

why.title: Built by a dubbing enthusiast, for everyone.
why.body: LibreRythmo came from one observation: rythmo band tools were either dated, clunky, or paid with a duration limit. And once the band was done, you still needed another app to record. Version 3 brings both into the same window, fast and entirely free.

points.title: Free forever
points.body: No subscription, no duration limit, no paywall. Open source, GPL-3 licensed.

points.title: Fast and light
points.body: Optimized to stay smooth even on an ordinary machine, from design to export.

points.title: Everything local
points.body: Transcription and voice removal run on your machine, with no connection and no account.

points.title: Made for creators
points.body: Built for fandub, associations and semi-pro work: it speaks the standards of the craft.

items.q: What is a rythmo band editor?
items.a: It is a tool to write text on a strip scrolling under the video and stretch each word so it sticks to the actor's lips: the standard dubbing technique. LibreRythmo does it for free on Windows, macOS and Linux, and it records the voices too.
Yes. It is entirely free and open source, GPL-3 licensed, with no subscription, no watermark and no duration limit. It will stay free forever.

items.q: Can I record my voice in it?
items.a: Yes, that is what the recording mode is for. Each character has their own track, takes stack up so you keep the best one, microphone latency is corrected, and an automatic voice chain cleans the sound with one button. Recordings mix into the exported video or come out as a per-character ZIP.

items.q: How do I act a character's part without hearing their voice?
items.a: The built-in voice remover makes an instrumental track, locally. When you mute a character, playback switches to it during their lines: their voice disappears, but the music, effects and other actors stay.

A composited, GPU-encoded MP4, with or without the band, with the chosen characters' voices mixed in. Also: a per-character ZIP of the recordings, PDF work documents, a DETX file (Joker and Cappella compatible) and subtitles (SRT / ASS / VTT).

items.q: Do transcription and voice removal need the Internet?
items.a: No, both run entirely on your machine, with no account and no connection. Nothing ships by default: engines and models install in one click from Settings, only when you need them.
Windows (installer or portable zip), macOS (Apple Silicon .dmg) and Linux (AppImage, .deb and .pacman). The interface is available in English, French and Spanish.
Yes. LibreRythmo builds a cached 720p proxy in the background so heavy 4K and HEVC sources stay smooth while editing, and regenerates the export from the full-quality original.

items.q: Is it a good alternative to paid dubbing tools?
items.a: Yes. LibreRythmo speaks standard formats like DETX, exports professional work documents and covers voice recording. It fits amateur, fandub and semi-pro workflows, without the cost or duration limits of paid or online tools.
